scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2,
PC5 at 10.5.0.5) say they cannot reach anything outside their
own subnet. They can still ping each other. Campus 2 VLAN 6
users (PC3, PC4) are unaffected and have full connectivity.
Identify the fault.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br_v5 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v5 SVI (10.5.0.254/24)
Mechanism: sshswitch is the multilayer switch that provides
  L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200. PCs in
  VLAN 5 (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) use 10.5.0.254 as their default
  gateway. When the br_v5 bridge interface goes down, the
  SVI IP becomes unreachable; packets from PCs to off-subnet
  destinations have no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
  unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v5 bridge interface is administratively down
  on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-device: sshswitch (not the access switch switch4)

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: the Layer-3 gateway interface for Campus 2 VLAN 5 on sshswitch (Linux bridge br_v5 providing 10.5.0.254/24). Mechanism: VLAN 5 hosts (10.5.0.0/24) can switch locally on switch4 so intra-subnet pings work, but their default gateway 10.5.0.254 does not respond. From pc1, ping to 10.5.0.254 is 100% loss despite a valid default route via 10.5.0.254. On sshswitch, the SVI/bridge for VLAN 5 is present with IP 10.5.0.254/24, but the bridge itself is administratively down, so it neither bridges nor ARPs, making the gateway unreachable while same-subnet traffic remains unaffected. Localization: sshswitch shows br_v5 in DOWN state while the equivalent VLAN 6 bridge (br_v6 at 10.6.0.254/24) is UP and operating, matching the report that VLAN 6 users are unaffected. Evidence: ip a on sshswitch shows “8: br_v5 … state DOWN … inet 10.5.0.254/24”, whereas br_v6 is “state UP.” pc1 cannot ping 10.5.0.254, confirming gateway unreachability. Root cause: The VLAN 5 bridge interface br_v5 on sshswitch was left administratively down. Corrective fix: Bring up the gateway bridge and ensure it is enabled at boot: ip link set br_v5 up; verify member ports (eth0.5, bond0.5) remain enslaved; optionally restart the switch’s network service to persist. After br_v5 is UP, hosts in 10.5.0.0/24 should reach outside networks again.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-device: sshswitch (not the access switch switch4)
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly localizes the fault to sshswitch (states br_v5 on sshswitch is DOWN and contrasts with br_v6 on sshswitch), not switch4.
The agent explicitly names the VLAN 5 SVI as br_v5 (10.5.0.254) on sshswitch as the affected component.
The report explicitly identifies VLAN 5 (br_v5) as down and states VLAN 6 (br_v6) is up and unaffected, distinguishing the two VLAN scopes.
Recommends bringing the bridge up with 'ip link set br_v5 up' and ensuring it remains enabled, which matches the expected fix.

The agent demonstrated that VLAN-5 hosts have a valid default route but cannot reach 10.5.0.254 (pc1 ping failed and neighbor table shows no ARP for .254), and concluded the bridge SVI on sshswitch is administratively down — a plausible cause — but the investigation log as shown does not explicitly include the sshswitch ip/link output proving br_v5 is in DOWN state nor verification of member ports.
